thread:
anya: PM asked for a tiny 'routing impact probe' in the console so teams can quickly simulate shifting X% traffic to a cheaper/quantized model and preview token-level cost + cache-credit effects before creating a canary. Can we scope an MVP?
sam: Yes. Minimal inputs: model/alt_model, route, reroute_pct, per-token price table (we have this), seq_len bucket fractions (fixed buckets), and current cache_hit_rate. We should avoid per-tenant minute-level data.
carl: Telemetry constraint: our trace sampling is low but router already emits counters. Proposal: router emits 1m rollups keyed by model+route+env with fields: token_count, cache_prefix_hits, seq_buckets (4 fixed buckets), p50/p95 latency. These rollups keep cardinality low.
divya: Backend plan: materialize the last N minutes of rollups (fast store TTL 1h) and build a lightweight sim service that reads the latest MV slice and applies math to estimate cost delta and CI. Fast path: use last-5m MV for sub-second responses; accurate path: aggregate longer window for smaller CI.
ux-izzy: UX: small inline card on route page: slider for reroute %, toggle prefetch/caching, and a small dropdown for preset scenarios (e.g., "shift 20% to small-quant"). Show three compact numbers: estimated_cost_delta, estimated_latency_delta, expected_cache_savings, plus a tiny confidence band. Add "Explain" that lists top-3 drivers. Include CTA "Apply as canary" to prefill rollout wizard.
sam: API sketch (JSON contract): POST /api/sim/v2/route-impact
request body example:
{
  "model": "redwood-7b-8bit",
  "alt_model": "redwood-7b-quant",
  "route": "us-west-1/low-latency",
  "reroute_pct": 30,
  "window_minutes": 60,
  "seq_len_buckets": [[0,64,0.55],[65,256,0.3],[257,1024,0.1],[1025,8192,0.05]],
  "cache_override": 0.12,
  "batch_size_hint": 8
}
response example:
{
  "predicted_cost_delta": -28.4,
  "predicted_tokens_impacted": 87432,
  "predicted_cache_savings": 3.6,
  "confidence_interval": [-33.1, -23.7],
  "top_drivers": ["cache_hit_rate","median_seq_len","per_token_price"],
  "assumptions": ["uses last-5m MV","extrapolates to window_minutes"]
}
carl: Important ops notes: do not index MV by tenant. Store only model+route+env to limit cardinality. For tenant-scoped previews, use sampled tenant-level counters or allow tenant_override input but compute on best-effort. Also emit sim_request metrics for service health.
divya: Validation/monitoring: run daily batch to compute sim_error = abs(predicted - actual)/actual per model and surface top offenders. If median sim_error > 25% for 3 days, pause expanding beta. Store only aggregated validation stats (daily per-model percentiles) to avoid cardinality blowup.
ux-izzy: UX detail: show a tiny sparkline of past sim_error on the card so customers can inspect reliability. Also label results as "estimate" and surface assumptions. Presets should include recommended canary percent & eval window.
sam: Implementation tasks: 1) router MV proto + emitter, 2) MV store & roller job (5m frequency), 3) sim service + auth, 4) console widget + gating + metrics for sim_error. Rough estimate: 2 engs 4-6 sprints for high-quality product; MVP (last-5m on-demand) ~3 weeks with one engineer.
anya: Security: gate feature to platform_admins and beta orgs. Redact raw token counts for org viewers that don't own the data (show percentages instead). Also ensure the sim endpoint requires console-service role.
infra-bot: created ticket RIP-1024 assigned to sam/carl. CI pipeline job 6201 queued. :gear:
divya: One more detail: to compute CI quickly we can bootstrap variance from minute-to-minute MV across the last N minutes rather than full sampling. That keeps compute light. Also limit seq_len bucket count to 4 to keep payloads small.
carl: Agree. Emit MV schema with fixed buckets [0-64,65-256,257-1024,>1024] as floats summing to 1. Keep p50/p95 for latency and a cached_prefix_hit_rate float.
ux-izzy: For the "Apply as canary" flow, the UI should prefill the rollout with suggested percent (from the preset) and an evaluation metric (cost delta + latency threshold). Permission check on apply.
anya: OK. @sam @carl please post proto PR for emitter + API contract by EOD. I'll coordinate with PM for beta org list and acceptance criteria. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
